title: Both Core Spell Teams must agree on the implementation proposal for any novel item
content:
For novel Spell items, A.1.10.2.3.3.2.3 provides that the Core Spell Teams conduct a technical feasibility analysis and develop an implementation proposal, and that "one Spell Team may take the lead, or both teams may work in parallel and reconcile approaches. **Both Spell Teams must agree on the implementation proposal.**"

The flexible part is who does the work; the fixed part is that both teams must sign. That converts the second team from a reviewer into a veto-holder. A reviewer with concerns can be overruled by a schedule; a party whose agreement is a precondition cannot.

The parallel-and-reconcile option is stronger still — two independent derivations of the same solution, compared afterwards. Divergence in the results is itself information about where the problem is underspecified, which review of a single design cannot surface.

This is the same insight applied to design that A.1.10.2.4.3.2.3 applies to arithmetic (two parties independently summing transfer totals): where an error would be expensive and hard to detect by inspection, Sky pays for duplicate independent work rather than for more careful single work. Sky deliberately maintains two Core Spell Teams, and this clause is part of what that redundancy is for.
description: Unanimity between two independent teams, not a lead team's sign-off: they may work in parallel and reconcile approaches, so a novel design must survive being derived twice.
